dedupe_keys.name: rogers national outage of 8 july 2022 crtc commissioned resiliency assessment xona partners

description: This post-event analysis is the assessment of Rogers' networks for resiliency and reliability that the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission commissioned from the consultancy Xona Partners after the nationwide Rogers outage of 8 July 2022. The outage lasted from 04:58 EDT on 8 July to about 07:00 EDT on 9 July, as services were gradually restored, and cut wireless and wireline services for more than 12 million customers, including 911 access, Interac debit and e-transfer payments and institutional customers providing critical services. The report, dated 12 December 2023 and released with an executive summary in July 2024 (a 67-page report and a 16-page summary, in English and French), found that staff removing an access-control policy filter from distribution routers during a configuration change flooded the IP core network with routing information and crashed it, that change management failed to flag the error, and that overload-protection mechanisms would have prevented it; it made further recommendations that Rogers confirmed it has implemented. Coverage: Canada-wide, one event. Format and access: PDF and HTML on the Government of Canada publications site and the CRTC website, free of charge under Crown copyright; the full report is redacted. Caveats: sensitive details are removed; it analyses one operator. Simulation uses: a reference case for cascading failure in an IP core network, dependency of payments and emergency services on one carrier, resilience planning and emergency response. Related records: the Optus 2023 outage review describes a similar routing overload, and Cloudflare Radar and IODA recorded the traffic loss.
